text: Thursday evening, the drive together into Tavistock
why: It is Thursday, they reached Tavistock in the evening, and they are now driving back into Tavistock together.

text: Why was the favourite made away with? — nobody meant to carry him off: he was led out to be harmed and got loose
id: q.why_taken=nobody meant to carry him off: he was led out to be harmed and got loose
why: Holmes asked why the thief did not harm the horse in the stable, and he showed the horse wandered alone afterwards. This makes the idea worth considering.

text: Why did Straker go out to the stables at one in the morning? — to do something to the horse himself
id: q.straker_reason=to do something to the horse himself
why: The story gives reasons to suspect Straker: the delicate cataract knife, the odd milliner's bill, Mrs. Straker's denial of the dress, Holmes asking for his photograph, and the lame sheep.

text: Why did Straker have the small knife with him? — to make some fine cut on the horse
id: q.knife=to make some fine cut on the horse
why: Holmes stresses the knife is meant for very delicate work and is strange to carry on a rough errand. That invites this guess.

text: What has lamed three of the sheep in the paddock? — someone cut their legs on purpose, practising for the horse
id: q.sheep_lame=someone cut their legs on purpose, practising for the horse
why: Holmes eagerly ties the lame sheep at King's Pyland to the case, and a delicate knife has already been found. Deliberate harm as practice is a guess a reader could fairly make.

text: Who lamed the sheep in the paddock?
why: This is a plain question raised by the lame sheep and Holmes's interest in them.

text: Who lamed the sheep in the paddock? — nobody: it is a natural ailment
id: q.who_lamed_sheep=nobody: it is a natural ailment
why: A natural ailment is the obvious ordinary explanation for lame sheep.

text: Who lamed the sheep in the paddock? — someone else at King's Pyland
why: This is an open, reasonable possibility, since the sheep are kept in the King's Pyland paddock.
